verses.1: When Jesus came down from the mountain, crowds followed him.
verses.2: Then a leper approached and worshipped him, saying, "Lord, if you are willing, you can make me clean."
verses.3: Jesus stretched out his hand and touched him, saying, "I am willing. Be cleansed." Immediately the leprosy left him.
verses.4: Then Jesus said to him, "See that you say nothing to anyone, but go, show yourself to the priest and offer the gift that Moses commanded, as a testimony to them."
verses.5: When he entered Capernaum, a centurion approached, pleading with him,
verses.6: saying, "Lord, my servant is lying in my house paralyzed, suffering greatly."
verses.7: Jesus said to him, "I will come and heal him."
verses.8: But the centurion responded, "Lord, I am not worthy to have you come under my roof. Just say the word, and my servant will be healed.
verses.9: For I myself am a man under authority, with soldiers under my command. I tell one, 'Go,' and he goes; another, 'Come,' and he comes; and to my slave, 'Do this,' and he does it."
verses.10: When Jesus heard this, he was astonished and said to those following him, "Truly I tell you, I have not found such great faith in anyone in Israel.
verses.11: I say to you that many will come from east and west and recline at table with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob in the kingdom of heaven,
verses.12: while the children of the kingdom will be thrown into the outer darkness, where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth."
verses.13: Then Jesus said to the centurion, "Go; let it be done for you as you have believed." And at that moment the servant was healed.
verses.14: When Jesus entered Peter's house, he saw his mother-in-law lying ill with a fever.
verses.15: He touched her hand, and the fever left her, and she rose and began to serve him.
verses.16: When evening came, many who were possessed by demons were brought to him, and he drove out the spirits with a word and healed all who were sick,
verses.17: so that what was spoken by the prophet Isaiah might be fulfilled: "He took up our infirmities and bore our diseases."
verses.18: Seeing the crowds around him, Jesus told them to go to the other side.
verses.19: Then a scribe approached and said to him, "Teacher, I will follow you wherever you go."
verses.20: Jesus said to him, "Foxes have dens and birds of the sky have nests, but the Son of Man has nowhere to lay his head."
verses.21: Another of the disciples said to him, "Lord, let me go first and bury my father."
verses.22: But Jesus said to him, "Follow me, and leave the dead to bury their own dead."
verses.23: When he got into a boat, his disciples followed him.
verses.24: Then a great storm arose on the sea, so that the boat was being swamped by the waves, but Jesus was sleeping.
verses.25: They came to him and woke him, saying, "Lord, save us! We are perishing!"
verses.26: He said to them, "Why are you so afraid, you of little faith?" Then he rose and rebuked the winds and the sea, and there was a great calm.
verses.27: The men were astonished and said, "What kind of man is this, that even the winds and the sea obey him?"
verses.28: When he arrived at the other side in the region of the Gerasenes, two men who were demon-possessed came out from the tombs, so violent that no one could pass by that road.
verses.29: They cried out, saying, "What do you have to do with us, Son of God? Have you come here to torment us before the time?"
verses.30: Now there was a large herd of pigs feeding some distance away.
verses.31: The demons were pleading with him, "If you cast us out, send us into the herd of pigs."
verses.32: He said to them, "Go." And they came out and went into the pigs. The whole herd rushed down the cliff into the sea and drowned.
verses.33: The shepherds fled, and going into the city they told everything about the demon-possessed men.
verses.34: Then the whole city came out to meet Jesus, and seeing him, they begged him to leave their region.

notes:
Notes
- v. 11: "many will come from east and west" – the translation of "ἀπὸ ἀνατολῶν καὶ δυσμῶν" follows the direction terms as "east and west" rather than "Mena and Dus" (ancient Greek terms).
- v. 20: "Foxes have dens and birds of the sky have nests" – the phrase "birds of the sky" is used to clarify the meaning of "πετεινὰ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ," which literally means "birds of heaven."
- v. 22: "leave the dead to bury their own dead" – the translation of "ἄφες τοὺς νεκροὺς θάψαι τοὺς ἑαυτῶν νεκρούς" is rendered to maintain clarity and natural English expression.

[2] Then a leper approached and worshipped him, saying, "Lord, if you are willing, you can make me clean."
[3] Jesus stretched out his hand and touched him, saying, "I am willing. Be cleansed." Immediately the leprosy left him.
[4] Then Jesus said to him, "See that you say nothing to anyone, but go, show yourself to the priest and offer the gift that Moses commanded, as a testimony to them."
[5] When he entered Capernaum, a centurion approached, pleading with him,
[6] saying, "Lord, my servant is lying in my house paralyzed, suffering greatly."
[7] Jesus said to him, "I will come and heal him."
[8] But the centurion responded, "Lord, I am not worthy to have you come under my roof. Just say the word, and my servant will be healed.
[9] For I myself am a man under authority, with soldiers under my command. I tell one, 'Go,' and he goes; another, 'Come,' and he comes; and to my slave, 'Do this,' and he does it."
[10] When Jesus heard this, he was astonished and said to those following him, "Truly I tell you, I have not found such great faith in anyone in Israel.
[11] I say to you that many will come from east and west and recline at table with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob in the kingdom of heaven,

[13] Then Jesus said to the centurion, "Go; let it be done for you as you have believed." And at that moment the servant was healed.
[14] When Jesus entered Peter's house, he saw his mother-in-law lying ill with a fever.
[15] He touched her hand, and the fever left her, and she rose and began to serve him.
[16] When evening came, many who were possessed by demons were brought to him, and he drove out the spirits with a word and healed all who were sick,
[17] so that what was spoken by the prophet Isaiah might be fulfilled: "He took up our infirmities and bore our diseases."
[18] Seeing the crowds around him, Jesus told them to go to the other side.
[19] Then a scribe approached and said to him, "Teacher, I will follow you wherever you go."
[20] Jesus said to him, "Foxes have dens and birds of the sky have nests, but the Son of Man has nowhere to lay his head."
[21] Another of the disciples said to him, "Lord, let me go first and bury my father."
[22] But Jesus said to him, "Follow me, and leave the dead to bury their own dead."
[23] When he got into a boat, his disciples followed him.
[24] Then a great storm arose on the sea, so that the boat was being swamped by the waves, but Jesus was sleeping.

[27] The men were astonished and said, "What kind of man is this, that even the winds and the sea obey him?"
[28] When he arrived at the other side in the region of the Gerasenes, two men who were demon-possessed came out from the tombs, so violent that no one could pass by that road.
[29] They cried out, saying, "What do you have to do with us, Son of God? Have you come here to torment us before the time?"
[30] Now there was a large herd of pigs feeding some distance away.
[31] The demons were pleading with him, "If you cast us out, send us into the herd of pigs."

[33] The shepherds fled, and going into the city they told everything about the demon-possessed men.
[34] Then the whole city came out to meet Jesus, and seeing him, they begged him to leave their region.
